name: ink
title: AMNT UI (Ink)
description: The whole Ink design system: 50+ components, tokens, 339 icons, app shells. Next.js + Tailwind 3.3+ or 4.
docs: Easiest: npx amnt-ui add (wires Tailwind and globals.css for you). By hand: npm i -D tailwindcss-animate @tailwindcss/typography. Tailwind 4: make tailwind.config.ts with `presets: [ink]` (import ink from './src/tailwind.preset') and content ['./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'], then at the top of globals.css: @import '../ui/tokens/tokens.css'; @import '../ui/tokens/legacy.css'; @import '../ui/ui.css'; @import 'tailwindcss'; @config '../../tailwind.config.ts'. Tailwind 3: add the preset and the three @imports. Full steps: github.com/amntio/amnt-ui#install

/**
 * Google's "G". Its four colours are Google's brand, not ours, and their
 * sign-in branding rules require them unchanged, so they are the one set of
 * hex values a sign-in button may carry. Sized like an M3 button icon (18dp).
 *
 * The four paths here form the G together - each colour fills one section of
 * the letter. The old version painted four quadrants of a 48x48 square and
 * showed up on the button as yellow/red/green/blue chunks.
 */
export function GoogleMark({ className }: { className?: string }) {
    return (
        <svg aria-hidden viewBox="0 0 48 48" className={className ?? "h-[1.125rem] w-[1.125rem] shrink-0"}>

}

/** * The M3 state layer and focus ring — the one implementation for the system. * * M3 has no hover colours. It has one mechanism: the component's own content * colour laid over it at a fixed opacity (8% hover, 10% focus, 10% pressed, * 16% dragged). The CSS is in `src/ui/ui.css`; this file is only the names, so * a component never types a class string by hand and a grep finds every user. * * ⚠️ Nothing outside `src/ui` may write a hover colour. If a surface needs a * hover it does not have, give it `interactive()` — do not invent a `hover:bg-…`. */ /** Container + state layer + focus ring. What every clickable thing gets. */ export const interactive = (opts?: { inverse?: boolean }) => `m3-state ${opts?.inverse ? "m3-focus-inverse" : "m3-focus"} outline-none`; /** The state layer alone — for a row that draws its own focus treatment. */ export const stateLayer = "m3-state"; /** The focus ring alone — for something that must not tint on hover. */ export const focusRing = "m3-focus"; /** M3 disabled: content at 38%, no pointer events. */ export const disabledStyles = "disabled:opacity-[0.38] disabled:pointer-events-none aria-disabled:opacity-[0.38] aria-disabled:pointer-events-none"; /** * The M3 48dp touch target, kept off the visual box. * * A 40dp icon button still has to be 48dp to the finger. Padding would grow * the button and break the layout, so the hit area is a transparent * pseudo-element centred on it instead. */ export const touchTarget = "relative before:absolute before:left-1/2 before:top-1/2 before:h-touch before:w-touch before:-translate-x-1/2 before:-translate-y-1/2 before:content-['']"; /** * Lift — the hover an ELEVATED thing gets: it rises 2px, gains one shadow * step, and its container steps to `surface-container-high` under the M3 * state layer. A static grid of cards becomes one that answers the pointer * (owner, 2026-09-26: "when you hover, the colour changes and you feel it is * alive"). * * 2026-09-28: the corner no longer morphs and the card no longer flashes * `primary-container`. A radius animating out of 9999px/12px glitches, and a * grid of cards turning purple one by one under the cursor fought every * other colour on the page (owner: "effects ... all need to be in harmony"). * The step is a neutral surface one; the accent stays with the actions. * * Only transform, shadow and background move - no reflow - and it all stops * under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Use on a card or a tile that opens * something. A row inside a list uses `interactive()` alone. * Children can answer too: it is `group/card`, so an icon plate inside can * `group-hover/card:bg-primary-container`. */ export const lift = "group/card m3-state m3-focus outline-none cursor-pointer " + /* `transform`, not `translate`: Tailwind 3.3's `-translate-y-*` writes `transform`, so the old list never animated the rise - it snapped (found 2026-09-29). The rise rides M3's default spatial spring. */ "transition-[box-shadow,transform,background-color] duration-spring-spatial ease-spring-spatial " + "hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:bg-surface-container-high hover:shadow-level-2 " + "focus-within:bg-surface-container-high focus-within:shadow-level-2 " + "motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:hover:translate-y-0"; /** * Reveal — the hover a picture gets: the image scales inside its own frame * while the frame stays put. Put this on the WRAPPER around the , not on * the card: transforming the card moves its badges and labels with it. * * The parent needs `group` and `overflow-hidden`. */ export const reveal = "transition-transform duration-medium1 ease-emphasized-decelerate " + "group-hover:scale-[1.03] motion-reduce:transform-none motion-reduce:transition-none";

/**
 * Material Symbols Rounded 400 — the one icon set (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md law 6).
 *
 *   import { Search, Close } from "@/ui/symbols";
 *   <Icon icon={Search} />
 *
 * Exports keep their lucide names on purpose: migrating a file is one import
 * line, not a rewrite of every call site in it. Each export is a plain object
 * of path data, so a route is only charged for the icons it draws — all 141
 * together would be 23 KB gz, and no route draws 141.
 *
 * Need one that is not here? Add the lucide name and the Material Symbols name
 * to `scripts/icon-map.json` and run `npm run icons:build`. Never hand-edit
 * the generated file, and never paste an SVG into a page.
 */
export * from "./primitives/symbols.generated";

/**
 * Brand-colour starting points for a collection website
 *
 * A seed is ONE colour. Google's Material colour maths turns it into the whole
 * light + dark scheme, so a creator picks a mood and
 * every button, chip and surface follows. Hex lives here, in the design
 * system, and nowhere in the feature.
 */
import { scheme } from "./tokens";

export const SITE_SEED_DEFAULT: string = scheme.seed;

 * build time. `npm run tokens:build` writes `tokens.css` and
 * `tokens.generated.json`; `tailwind.config.ts` reads this file directly.

 * Pinned so a library update can never silently repaint the product. M3

 * spec M3 ships today, and we say which one in writing.

    contrast: 0,

     * ⚠️ The `var()` carries its own fallback on purpose. A custom property
     * whose value contains an UNRESOLVABLE `var()` is invalid at computed-value
     * time — it does not fall back to the rest of the list, it computes to
     * nothing and inherits as nothing, and every page silently renders in
     * Times. That shipped once, on 2026-09-20, because `--font-brand` was on
     * <body> while this token is declared on `:root`. The class now lives on
     * <html>; this fallback is the second lock, so the same mistake degrades to

/**
 * The M3 type scale, all fifteen roles. Sizes are the spec's, in rem at a
 * 16px root.
 *
 * AMNT difference (recorded per law 2): the three Display sizes are fluid
 * between 360px and 1280px. 57px display type on a 360px phone is unusable,
 * and M3's own adaptive guidance is to step type down on compact windows — a
 * clamp is that, expressed once instead of at three breakpoints.
 *
 * AMNT addition (2026-10-03): `display-xl`, the page hero's h1 only - bigger
 * and bold, M3 Expressive's "emphasized" display (owner: the hero title must
 * be bold, with a nice shape). 44px on a phone, 76px on a desktop.
 *
 * AMNT difference (2026-10-04): weight and tracking are not M3's.
 *
 *   M3 sets every Display, Headline and Title role at weight 400. That is
 *   right for an Android system UI, where a heading is usually alone on a
 *   row and size alone carries the hierarchy. It is wrong here: at 24px a
 *   400 headline is indistinguishable from body text, so a dense page has no
 *   visible hierarchy at all. Headings are 600.
 *
 *   One rule, no optical compensation. Big apps (Vercel, Linear, Stripe)
 *   run a uniform 600 across their display/headline range rather than
 *   stepping weight down as size grows; stepping it down reads inconsistent
 *   rather than refined (a 500 display-lg next to a 600 display-sm makes
 *   the larger size look lighter than the smaller). `display-xl` is 800 -
 *   the page hero only, owner's pick - heavier than the rest on purpose.
 *
 *   Tracking is the spec's px value converted to em, except that headings
 *   get NEGATIVE tracking and body loses most of its positive tracking.
 *   M3's body-large is +0.031em, which is a lot on Figtree: Figtree is a
 *   wide geometric face, so the spec's letterspacing opens it further and
 *   running text reads airy instead of solid. Headings tighten as they grow
 *   (bigger type needs less air), body sits near zero, and labels keep M3's
 *   positive tracking because small caps-like text genuinely needs it.
 *
 *   This also fixes an outright inversion in the spec's scale: M3 has
 *   `title-lg` (22px) at 400 and `title-md` (16px) at 500, so the LARGER
 *   title rendered LIGHTER than the smaller one. Both are 600 now.
 */

    "headline-md": { size: "1.5rem", line: "2rem", weight: 600, tracking: "-0.02em" },
    "headline-sm": { size: "1.25rem", line: "1.75rem", weight: 600, tracking: "-0.015em" },

    "title-lg": { size: "1.0625rem", line: "1.625rem", weight: 600, tracking: "-0.01em" },
